title: Google's Open Knowledge Format: A Working Reference
description: What the OKF v0.2 specification actually says, what its own bundles reveal, and how to write YAML frontmatter that survives contact with a parser.

scope.objective: Establish what OKF v0.2 specifies, measure how far its own reference bundles follow it, and set out YAML frontmatter practice that survives real parsers.
covers: the specification text, section by section
the provenance, trust, and lifecycle model
YAML frontmatter mechanics and best practices
a measured conformance audit of the four shipped bundles
comparison with adjacent formats and standards
excludes: running the reference attester, which needs billed BigQuery credentials
any production OKF bundle, none of which were available
Google Cloud commercial terms for Knowledge Catalog
scope.evidenceBoundary: The specification, reference implementation, and four sample bundles at commit 374e0bc, plus public secondary coverage read on 2026-08-13.

glossary.definition: Who or what did something. Written as human:alice, process:nightly-job, or agent_name/version.
Checking that a single run produced its number the sanctioned way. Happens at runtime, on every call, and is never stored in the bundle.
A concept holding the one approved way to calculate a value, so a reader can confirm an agent ran it rather than improvising.
Plain deterministic code, with no AI model involved, that inspects a receipt and returns pass or fail.
YAML written one key per line, indented. The opposite of flow style.
Everything in a concept file after the frontmatter. Ordinary Markdown.
A directory of OKF files. The unit you ship.
An invisible marker some editors put at the start of a file. Breaks readers that expect --- as the first characters.
The - or + after a YAML block scalar marker, controlling trailing newlines. `\
One unit of knowledge, stored as one Markdown file.
The file's path inside the bundle with .md removed.
The three-rule test in section 11: frontmatter parses, type is non-empty, reserved files follow their format.
An objective fact about a source (author, usage_count, last_modified) from which a reader infers trust. OKF records signals, never a score.
status: deprecated. Kept so old links and reports work; no longer current.
You can see line by line what changed between two versions. The reason the format is text.
Instructions or code that runs a computation and returns a receipt.
Compact YAML using { } and [ ] on one line. Used throughout OKF's examples.
A block of YAML at the top of a Markdown file, fenced by ---. No formal standard defines it.
YAML guessing what a value means from how it looks. The root of most YAML surprises.
index.md. Lists a directory's contents so a reader can see what exists before opening anything. Carries no frontmatter, except okf_version at the bundle root.
The international date and time format, for example 2026-05-28T14:30:00Z.
Whether a concept is current: status and stale_after.
An ordinary Markdown link between concepts. Asserts a relationship without saying what kind.
log.md. History of changes, newest first, grouped by ISO date.
YAML 1.1 reading NO as the boolean false. Named for the country code.
Base 8. YAML 1.1 reads a leading zero as octal, so 02134 becomes 1116.
Letting a reader see what is available before opening it. The reason index.md exists.
The set of sources a concept derives from. Recorded in sources.
Evidence a run returns, shaped by executor.receipt. A runtime object, never stored.
index.md and log.md. Cannot be used for concepts.
Reading a file and writing it back. Lossless if formatting survives; OKF's reference writer is not lossless.
How a computation is executed: bigquery, dbt, python. Decides what parameters mean.
Base 60. YAML 1.1 reads 22:53 as 1373.
Material a concept derives from, internal or external.
Today's date is on or after stale_after.
One of unverified, machine-confirmed, or human-reviewed. Calculated from verified on read, never written into a file.
The field recording who confirmed a concept's content against its sources. Distinct from who wrote it.
The text format used for frontmatter. Version 1.1 (2005) and 1.2 (2009) differ in ways that matter; PyYAML still implements 1.1.

unestablished.question: Any organisation outside Google publishing a production OKF bundle
unestablished.status: Not found. Every bundle located was a sample, a demo, or a test fixture

unestablished.question: Whether OKF ingestion is generally available in a Google product
unestablished.status: Not confirmed. The launch blog says Knowledge Catalog "now ingests OKF"; no public documentation of a generally available capability was found

unestablished.question: A published roadmap for v0.3
unestablished.status: Not found. The only forward-looking statement is the deferred list in spec section 12

unestablished.question: Independent benchmarks of agent accuracy with and without an OKF bundle
unestablished.status: Not found. The premise that curated context improves agent answers is asserted, not measured, in every source located

limitations: The specification moved from v0.1 to v0.2 in six weeks; every statement here is a snapshot of commit 374e0bc.
Four sample bundles is a small sample, and all four are Google's own. The defect rates describe the examples, not production usage.
The audit checks structure, not whether the knowledge in a bundle is true.
Attestation behaviour was established by reading the reference attester, not by executing it.
Round-trip behaviour was measured for Python only; a JavaScript producer using js-yaml will differ.
